theoryOfChange: The Muslim Community Network (MCN) has a documented approach to measuring change, evidenced by its 'Our Impact' and 'Community Education' pages on its website. These pages detail program areas, activities, and measurable outcomes. For instance, the 'Our Impact' page highlights that 86.6% of participants reported increased understanding of Islam after diversity workshops, 92.8% reported proficiency in self-defense after training, and 100% reported proficiency in understanding protections under NYC's Human Rights Office after civic education. This demonstrates a structured approach to tracking the impact of their programs. The organization also mentions an 'FY25 Annual Report' and a 'Hate Crime Prevention Report' as documents detailing their work and impact.

strengths_deep_dive: The organization directs <cite id="5">81% of its spending directly to core programs</cite>, including civic education and community safety workshops in New York City [4], [5]. This level of operational spending meets established financial health benchmarks for advocacy nonprofits [5]. Furthermore, a <cite id="5">Charity Navigator score of 87.0/100</cite> reflects consistent accountability and financial reporting practices [5].
rich_narrative.summary: The Muslim Community Network is a New York-based organization focused on civic education, youth leadership, and community safety [4]. Founded in 2003, the charity works across local neighborhoods to strengthen leadership and increase Muslim participation in civic life [4]. In FY2025 filings, the organization reported <cite id="1">total revenue of $768,698</cite> sourced primarily through individual and institutional contributions [1]. Program activities are structured around key tracks, including the Impact Academy, Community Safety, and Immigrant Support [4]. Financial evaluation shows a <cite id="5">program expense ratio of 80.6%</cite>, which aligns closely with sector standards [5]. The organization maintains an explicit zakat policy and distributes funds across recognized charitable categories [2]. External evaluations include an <cite id="5">overall Charity Navigator score of 87.0/100</cite> alongside a Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid [5]. Governance oversight remains an area for development due to incomplete public board records [1]. Overall operations balance direct civic education initiatives with local community advocacy [4].
